```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
```

```{r load-arf}
if (requireNamespace("devtools", quietly = TRUE)) devtools::load_all(".") else library(ARF)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

This notebook runs dripARF on the mouse IP/Total Ribo-seq benchmark dataset using 18 mouse
ribosome structures from RCSB, plus the built-in mouse preset, and produces an ES2 heatmap
comparing RP enrichment signals across structures. It demonstrates both **Path 1** (built-in
mouse preset) and **Path 4** (custom PDB structures with sequence-alignment-based conversion
tables) from the ARF workflow described in the README.

---

# Settings

```{r settings}
mouse_rRNAs  <- "rRNAs/mouse_rRNAs.fa"
samples_file <- "test_data/Rpl10aRps25Rpl22_samples_mouse.tsv"
target_RPs   <- c("uL1", "eS25", "eL22")

comparisons <- list(
  c("uL1_FLAG",  "uL1_Total"),
  c("eS25_FLAG", "eS25_Total"),
  c("eL22_HA",   "eL22_Total"),
  c("uL1_FLAG",  "eL22_HA"),
  c("eS25_FLAG", "eL22_HA"),
  c("uL1_Total", "eS25_Total")
)
comp_labels <- sapply(comparisons, paste, collapse = "_vs_")

pdbs <- c(
  "31FX", "31FY", "31FZ", "9QZP",
  "9QWT", "9QQL", "9QQP", "9QSA",
  "9QOH", "7CPU", "7CPV",
  "7LS1", "7LS2"
)

base_dir <- "testrun/mouse_struct_cmp"
dir.create(base_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

---

# Helper functions: chain conversion table

> **Note on nomenclature generation.** The conversion table built below is written
> specifically for these 18 mouse ribosome structures. It is intended as a worked
> example and a starting point, not a general-purpose solution. For any new structure
> the generated mapping must be verified manually: chain descriptions vary across
> releases, some chains carry non-standard names, and fusion proteins or non-RP
> binders may receive ambiguous assignments. Always review the table before passing
> it to `ARF_parse_PDB_ribosome`.

For each structure a chain-to-RP mapping is built from the RCSB FASTA using two
complementary strategies:

1. **Greedy one-to-one sequence alignment** against a reference AAStringSet built from
   the three full mouse 80S structures (9QZP / 9QQL / 9QOH). A score matrix is built
   first using fast scoreOnly local alignments (BLOSUM62, gap open 10, gap extend 0.5).
   All (query chain, reference RP) pairs are then sorted by score descending. Walking
   from the top, a pair is accepted — and both the query chain and the reference RP are
   marked as assigned — when the full alignment PID meets or exceeds `min_pid` (default
   95 %). Each reference RP is assigned to at most one query chain, so in a monosome
   structure every RP appears at most once. PID is computed over the aligned region, so
   truncated or fusion chains (e.g. ubiquitin-RP fusions) still resolve correctly as
   long as the RP portion aligns well.
2. **Description string parsing** for chains with no alignment hit above the threshold.
   When the description contains "protein", "factor", or "initiator", the last
   whitespace-delimited token is taken as the RP name (RCSB convention places the RP
   name at the end: "60S ribosomal subunit protein **eL18**"). Otherwise the first
   token is used (e.g. "**RACK1** 40S ribosomal protein"). A `-like` suffix is stripped
   (e.g. `uL16-like` becomes `uL16`).

Chains that fail both strategies (zero-length sequence, non-RP ligands) are silently
dropped. rRNA chains are detected separately by "ribosomal RNA" in the description and
named `rRNA_28S`, `rRNA_18S`, `rRNA_5.8S`, `rRNA_5S`. Non-ribosomal RNA chains (mRNA,
tRNA) are excluded from both paths entirely.

```{r conversion-fn}
# Suppress cat() progress lines (e.g. "Reading the bedgraph file") while keeping
# message() output and the return value intact.
.silent <- function(x) {
  .val <- NULL
  invisible(capture.output(.val <- x))
  .val
}

extract_auth_chains <- function(chain_info) {
  parts    <- strsplit(chain_info, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  auth_ids <- vapply(trimws(parts), function(p) {
    if (grepl("auth", p, fixed = TRUE)) gsub(".*auth ([^]]+)\\].*", "\\1", p)
    else gsub("^Chains*\\s*", "", p)
  }, character(1))
  paste(trimws(auth_ids), collapse = ",")
}

# Build a named AAStringSet: one sequence per RP_new from 9QZP/9QQL/9QOH.
# Sequences are taken from whichever reference structure first provides a given RP.
build_ref_aa_seqs <- function(ref_pdbs   = c("9QZP", "9QQL", "9QOH"),
                               base_dir   = "testrun/mouse_struct_cmp",
                               all_pdb_rps_file = "data-raw/ALL_PDB_RPS_edited.csv") {
  all_rps <- read.table(all_pdb_rps_file, sep = ",", header = TRUE)
  ref_seqs <- list()
  for (pdb in ref_pdbs) {
    fasta_path  <- file.path(base_dir, pdb, paste0(pdb, ".fasta"))
    raw         <- Biostrings::readBStringSet(fasta_path)
    split_names <- strsplit(names(raw), "|", fixed = TRUE)
    chain_infos <- vapply(split_names, function(x) if (length(x)>=2L) x[[2L]] else "", character(1))
    chain_ids   <- vapply(chain_infos, extract_auth_chains, character(1))
    # For multi-copy entries take the first auth chain ID only
    first_chain <- sub(",.*", "", chain_ids)
    # Look up RP_new for each chain from the CSV (this PDB is now in there)
    pdb_rows    <- dplyr::filter(all_rps, PDB_id == pdb)
    # chain_info in CSV contains the full "Chain X[auth Y]" string; extract auth ID
    pdb_rows$auth_id <- sub(",.*", "",
                             vapply(pdb_rows$chain_info, extract_auth_chains, character(1)))
    for (i in seq_along(raw)) {
      cid  <- first_chain[i]
      rp   <- pdb_rows$RP_new[match(cid, pdb_rows$auth_id)]
      # keep only well-formed universal RP names (eL/uL/eS/uS + RACK1)
      if (!is.na(rp) && grepl("^[eu][LS][0-9]|^RACK1", rp) && !(rp %in% names(ref_seqs))) {
        ref_seqs[[rp]] <- as.character(raw[[i]])
      }
    }
  }
  Biostrings::AAStringSet(unlist(ref_seqs))
}

build_conversion_table <- function(fasta_path,
                                   ref_aa_seqs      = NULL,
                                   min_pid          = 95,
                                   all_pdb_rps_file = "data-raw/ALL_PDB_RPS_edited.csv",
                                   return_pid       = FALSE) {
  raw         <- Biostrings::readBStringSet(fasta_path)
  split_names <- strsplit(names(raw), "|", fixed = TRUE)
  tbl <- data.frame(
    ID          = vapply(split_names, `[[`, character(1), 1L),
    chain_info  = vapply(split_names, function(x) if (length(x)>=2L) x[[2L]] else "", character(1)),
    description = vapply(split_names, function(x) if (length(x)>=3L) x[[3L]] else "", character(1)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  tbl$chainID <- vapply(tbl$chain_info, extract_auth_chains, character(1))
  # ribosomal RNA chains: match "ribosomal RNA" or "rRNA" in the description
  is_rRNA     <- grepl("ribosomal RNA|rRNA", tbl$description, ignore.case = TRUE)
  # other RNA chains: mRNA, tRNA (incl. "Met-tRNA", "P/E tRNA" etc.) and any
  # description containing "RNA" that is not ribosomal RNA. "\bRNA\b" misses
  # "tRNA" because the word boundary fails before the "R", so match "RNA" and
  # "tRNA" separately. Nascent peptide chains are also excluded — they are not RPs.
  is_other_RNA <- grepl("RNA|tRNA", tbl$description, ignore.case = TRUE) & !is_rRNA
  is_nascent   <- grepl("nascent", tbl$description, ignore.case = TRUE)

  # --- rRNA rows: name by size (rRNA_28S, rRNA_18S, etc.) ----------------------
  # Use stringr::str_extract which returns NA for non-matches (unlike regmatches
  # which drops non-matching rows and causes vector-length mismatches).
  rRNA_rows <- tbl[is_rRNA, ]
  rRNA_rows$RP_name <- paste0("rRNA_",
    stringr::str_extract(rRNA_rows$description, "[0-9]+\\.?[0-9]*S"))
  rRNA_rows$RP_new  <- rRNA_rows$RP_name
  rRNA_rows <- rRNA_rows[, c("ID","RP_name","RP_new","chainID")]

  # --- protein rows ------------------------------------------------------------
  prot_tbl <- tbl[!is_rRNA & !is_other_RNA & !is_nascent, ]

  # Descriptions that must bypass alignment entirely — they produce false-positive
  # BLOSUM62 hits against real RPs (e.g. RACK1 -> eS31 at 80% PID).
  skip_aln_descs <- c("Elongation factor 2", "Receptor of activated protein C kinase 1")
  skip_aln_mask  <- prot_tbl$description %in% skip_aln_descs

  # Strategy 1: greedy one-to-one alignment against reference AAStringSet.
  # Each reference RP is assigned to at most one query chain, preventing multiple
  # chains in a monosome from all claiming the same top-scoring reference.
  # Step 1a: build score matrix (scoreOnly for speed).
  aln_rp     <- rep(NA_character_, nrow(prot_tbl))
  pid_records <- list()
  if (!is.null(ref_aa_seqs) && length(ref_aa_seqs) > 0 && nrow(prot_tbl) > 0) {
    query_seqs <- vector("list", nrow(prot_tbl))
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(prot_tbl))) {
      if (skip_aln_mask[i]) next
      query_seqs[[i]] <- tryCatch(
        Biostrings::AAString(as.character(raw[[which(tbl$ID == prot_tbl$ID[i])]])),
        error = function(e) NULL
      )
    }
    score_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = nrow(prot_tbl), ncol = length(ref_aa_seqs))
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(prot_tbl))) {
      if (skip_aln_mask[i]) next
      qs <- query_seqs[[i]]
      if (is.null(qs) || nchar(as.character(qs)) == 0L) next
      score_matrix[i, ] <- tryCatch(
        Biostrings::pairwiseAlignment(
          Biostrings::AAStringSet(rep(as.character(qs), length(ref_aa_seqs))),
          ref_aa_seqs,
          type = "local", substitutionMatrix = "BLOSUM62",
          gapOpening = 10, gapExtension = 0.5, scoreOnly = TRUE
        ),
        error = function(e) numeric(length(ref_aa_seqs))
      )
    }
    # Step 1b: greedy assignment — walk pairs from highest score downward;
    # assign only when both query and reference are still unassigned.
    assigned_q <- logical(nrow(prot_tbl))
    assigned_r <- logical(length(ref_aa_seqs))
    pairs <- which(score_matrix > 0, arr.ind = TRUE)
    if (nrow(pairs) > 0) {
      pairs <- pairs[order(score_matrix[pairs], decreasing = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]
      for (k in seq_len(nrow(pairs))) {
        qi <- pairs[k, 1L]; ri <- pairs[k, 2L]
        if (assigned_q[qi] || assigned_r[ri]) next
        qs <- query_seqs[[qi]]
        if (is.null(qs) || nchar(as.character(qs)) == 0L) next
        aln <- tryCatch(
          Biostrings::pairwiseAlignment(
            qs, ref_aa_seqs[[ri]],
            type = "local", substitutionMatrix = "BLOSUM62",
            gapOpening = 10, gapExtension = 0.5
          ),
          error = function(e) NULL
        )
        if (is.null(aln)) next
        pid_val <- Biostrings::pid(aln)
        if (!is.na(pid_val)) {
          pid_records[[length(pid_records)+1]] <- data.frame(
            RP = names(ref_aa_seqs)[ri], PID = pid_val, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
          )
          if (pid_val >= min_pid) {
            aln_rp[qi]     <- names(ref_aa_seqs)[ri]
            assigned_q[qi] <- TRUE
            assigned_r[ri] <- TRUE
            if (pid_val < 95)
              warning(sprintf(
                "Low-confidence assignment: chain %s -> %s (PID %.1f%%)",
                prot_tbl$ID[qi], names(ref_aa_seqs)[ri], pid_val
              ))
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }

  # Strategy 2: description string parsing fallback for chains with no alignment hit.
  # Full-description map handles entries whose generic last-word parsing would yield
  # a bare number (digit filter would then drop them). EF2 ends in "2"; RACK1 ends in "1".
  # Keys are the same as skip_aln_descs defined above.
  desc_name_map <- c("Elongation factor 2" = "EF2",
                     "Receptor of activated protein C kinase 1" = "RACK1",
                     "40S ribosomal protein S4, X isoform" = "eS4")
  # Generic rule: takes last token when description contains "protein"/"factor"/"initiator"
  # (RP name appears at the end in standard RCSB convention), otherwise first token.
  prot_last <- vapply(strsplit(prot_tbl$description, " "),
                      function(x) x[length(x)], character(1))
  desc_rp <- ifelse(
    grepl("protein|factor|initiator", prot_tbl$description),
    prot_last,
    vapply(strsplit(prot_tbl$description, " "), function(x) x[1L], character(1))
  )
  # Apply full-description overrides after generic parsing
  desc_rp <- ifelse(prot_tbl$description %in% names(desc_name_map),
                    desc_name_map[prot_tbl$description], desc_rp)
  # Remap human old-nomenclature names to the unified nomenclature.
  # Source: Ban group Tables 1a (SSU) and 1b (LSU), "Human Old name" column only.
  # https://bangroup.ethz.ch/research/nomenclature-of-ribosomal-proteins.html
  old_to_new <- c(
    # LSU
    L3="uL3",  L4="uL4",  L5="uL18", L6="eL6",
    L7="uL30", L7a="eL8", L8="uL2",  L9="uL6",
    L10="uL16", L10a="uL1", "L10-like"="uL16-like",
    L11="uL5",  L12="uL11", L13="eL13", L13a="uL13",
    L14="eL14", L15="eL15", L17="uL22", L18="eL18",
    L18a="eL20", L19="eL19", L21="eL21", L22="eL22",
    L23="uL14", L23a="uL23", L24="eL24", L26="uL24",
    L27="eL27", L27a="uL15", L28="eL28", L29="eL29",
    L30="eL30", L31="eL31", L32="eL32", L34="eL34",
    L35="uL29", L35a="eL33", L36="eL36", L36a="eL42",
    L37="eL37", L37a="eL43", L38="eL38", L39="eL39",
    "L39-like"="eL39-like", L40="eL40", L41="eS32",
    P0="uL10",
    # SSU
    SA="uS2",   S2="uS5",  S3="uS3",  S3a="eS1",  S4="eS4",
    S5="uS7",   S6="eS6",  S7="eS7",  S8="eS8",   S9="uS4",
    S10="eS10", S11="uS17", S12="eS12", S13="uS15", S14="uS11",
    S15="uS19", S15a="uS8", S16="uS9", S17="eS17", S18="uS13",
    S19="eS19", S20="uS10", S21="eS21", S23="uS12", S24="eS24",
    S25="eS25", S26="eS26", S27="eS27", "S27-like"="eS27-like",
    S27a="eS31", S28="eS28", S29="uS14", S30="eS30"
  )
  desc_rp <- ifelse(desc_rp %in% names(old_to_new), old_to_new[desc_rp], desc_rp)

  # Merge: Ban table description name wins; alignment fills where description fails
  resolved_rp <- ifelse(!is.na(desc_rp) & desc_rp != "", desc_rp, aln_rp)
  prot_rows <- data.frame(
    ID      = prot_tbl$ID,
    RP_name = resolved_rp,
    RP_new  = resolved_rp,
    chainID = prot_tbl$chainID,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  prot_rows <- prot_rows[!is.na(prot_rows$RP_name) & prot_rows$RP_name != "" &
                           !grepl("^[0-9]", prot_rows$RP_name), ]

  out <- dplyr::distinct(rbind(prot_rows, rRNA_rows))
  if (return_pid) {
    pid_df <- if (length(pid_records)) do.call(rbind, pid_records) else
      data.frame(RP = character(), PID = numeric(), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    return(list(table = out, pid_data = pid_df))
  }
  out
}
```

# Path 1 — Built-in mouse preset

Uses the built-in `mm` structural data (no PDB download needed).

```{r builtin-mm}
builtin_rds <- file.path(base_dir, "builtin_mm_results.rds")
if (!file.exists(builtin_rds)) {
  dir.create(file.path(base_dir, "builtin_mm"), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  res_builtin <- .silent(ARF::dripARF(
    samplesFile  = samples_file,
    rRNAs_fasta  = mouse_rRNAs,
    organism     = "mm",
    compare      = "group",
    comparisons  = comparisons,
    QCplot       = FALSE,
    ssRPSEAplots = FALSE,
    targetDir    = file.path(base_dir, "builtin_mm")
  ))
  saveRDS(res_builtin, builtin_rds)
}
results_list <- list(builtin_mm = readRDS(builtin_rds))
```

# Path 4 — Custom structure pipeline (requires internet)

For each PDB: download FASTA + CIF, build conversion table, compute RP–rRNA distances,
lift to mouse rRNA coordinates, generate RP proximity sets, run dripARF.
Results are cached as `.rds` files; re-knitting skips completed structures.

```{r custom-structures, message=TRUE}
# Build reference AAStringSet once from the 3 reference mouse 80S structures
ref_aa <- build_ref_aa_seqs(base_dir = base_dir)
message("Reference sequences built: ", length(ref_aa), " RPs")

for (pdb in pdbs) {
  outdir  <- file.path(base_dir, pdb)
  rds_out <- file.path(outdir, "dripARF_results.rds")

  if (file.exists(rds_out)) {
    cached <- readRDS(rds_out)
    if (!is.null(cached)) {
      results_list[[pdb]] <- cached
      message(pdb, ": loaded from cache.")
      next
    }
  }

  message("\n--- Processing ", pdb, " ---")
  dir.create(outdir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

  res <- tryCatch({
    # Download RCSB FASTA for chain mapping
    fasta_path <- file.path(outdir, paste0(pdb, ".fasta"))
    if (!file.exists(fasta_path))
      utils::download.file(
        paste0("https://www.rcsb.org/fasta/entry/", pdb),
        fasta_path, quiet = TRUE
      )

    conv_df <- build_conversion_table(fasta_path, ref_aa_seqs = ref_aa)

    # 7LS1: RCSB annotation error — chain TA (auth m2, 1871 nt 18S) is described
    # as "28S rRNA" in the FASTA, causing build_conversion_table to assign it
    # rRNA_28S. Correct it here before passing to the parser.
    if (pdb == "7LS1") {
      conv_df$RP_name[conv_df$chainID == "m2"] <- "rRNA_18S"
      conv_df$RP_new[conv_df$chainID  == "m2"] <- "rRNA_18S"
    }

    # Compute RP–rRNA distances
    cif_path  <- file.path(outdir, paste0(pdb, ".cif"))
    .silent(ARF::ARF_parse_PDB_ribosome(
      species                      = "mm",
      PDBid                        = pdb,
      PDB_file                     = if (file.exists(cif_path)) cif_path else NULL,
      rRNAs_file                   = NULL,
      download_directory           = outdir,
      out_prefix                   = file.path(outdir, "Ribosome.3D"),
      PDB_chains_2_RP_nomenclature = conv_df
    ))

    # Liftover to mouse rRNA coordinates.
    # auth→FASTA position correction is automatic via the rRNA_resno_map.csv written by parse.
    LO_df <- .silent(ARF::ARF_convert_Ribo3D_pos(
      source_distance_file = file.path(outdir, paste0("Ribosome.3D.", pdb, ".ARF.minimum_distances.csv")),
      source_rRNAs_fasta   = file.path(outdir, paste0(pdb, ".rRNAs.fasta")),
      target_species       = "mm",
      target_rRNAs_fasta   = mouse_rRNAs,
      type                 = "distances"
    ))

    # RP proximity sets from this structure
    gsea_sets_RP <- ARF::dripARF_get_RP_proximity_sets(
      RP_proximity_df   = LO_df,
      additional_RPcols = c(),
      rRNAs_fasta       = mouse_rRNAs
    )

    # Run dripARF for all comparisons in one call
    .silent(ARF::dripARF(
      samplesFile     = samples_file,
      rRNAs_fasta     = mouse_rRNAs,
      organism        = "mm",
      compare         = "group",
      comparisons     = comparisons,
      QCplot          = FALSE,
      ssRPSEAplots    = FALSE,
      targetDir       = outdir,
      gsea_sets_RP    = gsea_sets_RP,
      RP_proximity_df = LO_df
    ))
  }, error = function(e) {
    message(pdb, ": failed — ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  })

  saveRDS(res, rds_out)
  results_list[[pdb]] <- res
  if (!is.null(res)) message(pdb, ": done.") else message(pdb, ": skipped (error).")
}
```

# Chain-to-RP alignment identity

Sequence identity of each protein chain to its assigned reference RP, across all 18
structures. Only RPs with at least one alignment below 100% are shown; RPs that align
at 100% in every structure are omitted for clarity. The dashed line marks the 80% PID
threshold below which alignment-based assignment is rejected and description parsing
is used instead.

```{r pid-figure, fig.width=12, fig.height=9}
pid_rds <- file.path(base_dir, "pid_data.rds")
if (file.exists(pid_rds)) {
  pid_df <- readRDS(pid_rds)
} else {
  all_pid <- lapply(pdbs, function(pdb) {
    fasta_path <- file.path(base_dir, pdb, paste0(pdb, ".fasta"))
    if (!file.exists(fasta_path)) return(NULL)
    res <- build_conversion_table(fasta_path, ref_aa_seqs = ref_aa, return_pid = TRUE)
    if (nrow(res$pid_data) == 0) return(NULL)
    cbind(res$pid_data, PDB = pdb, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  })
  pid_df <- do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), all_pid))
  saveRDS(pid_df, pid_rds)
}

# Panel A: per-structure summary — number of assignments below 100% and below 95%
summ_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(pid_df$PDB), function(p) {
  d <- pid_df[pid_df$PDB == p, ]
  data.frame(PDB      = p,
             total    = nrow(d),
             lt100    = sum(d$PID < 100),
             lt95     = sum(d$PID < 95),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
summ_df$PDB <- factor(summ_df$PDB, levels = pdbs)

p_summary <- ggplot2::ggplot(summ_df, ggplot2::aes(x = PDB)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(ggplot2::aes(y = total), fill = "grey85") +
  ggplot2::geom_col(ggplot2::aes(y = lt100), fill = "#fdae61") +
  ggplot2::geom_col(ggplot2::aes(y = lt95),  fill = "#d73027") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Number of RPs",
                title = "Assignments per structure",
                subtitle = "Grey = total assigned; orange = PID < 100%; red = PID < 95%") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
  ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Panel B: jitter of only RPs with at least one alignment < 100% (excludes all-100% structures)
variable_rps <- unique(pid_df$RP[pid_df$PID < 100])
plot_df <- pid_df[pid_df$RP %in% variable_rps, ]
plot_df$RP      <- factor(plot_df$RP, levels = sort(unique(plot_df$RP)))
plot_df$subunit <- ifelse(grepl("^eS|^uS", plot_df$RP), "SSU", "LSU")

p_jitter <- ggplot2::ggplot(plot_df, ggplot2::aes(x = RP, y = PID, colour = subunit)) +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 95, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c(SSU = "#2166ac", LSU = "#d6604d"),
                               name = "Subunit") +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 20),
                               labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Percent identity",
                title = "Variable RP alignments",
                subtitle = sprintf("%d RPs with PID < 100%% in at least one structure",
                                   length(variable_rps))) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
  ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x  = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
                 panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                 legend.position = "top")

gridExtra::grid.arrange(p_summary, p_jitter, ncol = 1)
```

# ES2 heatmaps

A helper builds each heatmap from a chosen score column.

```{r es2-heatmap-fn}
make_es2_heatmap <- function(score_col, title, legend_label) {
  df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    lapply(names(results_list), function(struct) {
      res <- results_list[[struct]]
      if (is.null(res) || nrow(res) == 0) return(NULL)
      res |>
        dplyr::filter(Description %in% target_RPs, comp %in% comp_labels) |>
        dplyr::select(comp, Description, ES2 = dplyr::all_of(score_col)) |>
        dplyr::mutate(structure = struct)
    })
  )
  struct_order <- c("builtin_mm", pdbs)
  df$structure   <- factor(df$structure,   levels = rev(struct_order))
  df$Description <- factor(df$Description, levels = target_RPs)
  df$comp <- factor(df$comp, levels = comp_labels,
                    labels = gsub("_", " ", comp_labels))
  lim <- max(abs(df$ES2), na.rm = TRUE)
  ggplot(df, aes(x = Description, y = structure, fill = ES2)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(!is.na(ES2), sprintf("%.1f", ES2), "")),
              size = 2.8) +
    facet_wrap(~ comp, nrow = 1) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = "steelblue", mid = "white", high = "firebrick",
      midpoint = 0, limits = c(-lim, lim),
      na.value = "grey85", name = legend_label
    ) +
    scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
    labs(title = title,
         caption = "Rows: PDB structures. Columns: target RPs. Panels: IP vs Total comparisons.",
         x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(axis.text.x    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
          axis.text.y    = element_text(size = 9),
          strip.text     = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
          panel.grid     = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "right")
}
```

## ES2 (RPSEA NES z-score)

`RPSEA.NES_randZ`: NES normalised by the z-score of its randomised control distribution.

```{r es2-heatmap, fig.width=11, fig.height=8}
make_es2_heatmap("RPSEA.NES_randZ",
                 "dripARF ES2 across mouse ribosome structures",
                 "ES2\n(NES z-score)")
```

## ssRPSEA-corrected ES2

`weighted.RPSEA.NES_randZ`: ES2 weighted by the ssRPSEA score, correcting for transcript
abundance differences between IP and Total.

```{r es2-ssrpsea-heatmap, fig.width=11, fig.height=8}
make_es2_heatmap("weighted.RPSEA.NES_randZ",
                 "dripARF ssRPSEA-corrected ES2 across mouse ribosome structures",
                 "ssRPSEA ES2\n(weighted NES z-score)")
```

## Rank heatmap

Rank of each target RP within all RPs for that structure × comparison, ordered by ES2
descending (rank 1 = highest ES2). Grey = structure not yet run or RP absent.

```{r rank-heatmap, fig.width=11, fig.height=8}
rank_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(names(results_list), function(struct) {
    res <- results_list[[struct]]
    if (is.null(res) || nrow(res) == 0) return(NULL)
    do.call(rbind, lapply(comp_labels, function(cmp) {
      sub <- res[res$comp == cmp, ]
      sub <- sub[order(sub$RPSEA.NES_randZ, decreasing = TRUE), ]
      sub$rank <- seq_len(nrow(sub))
      sub[sub$Description %in% target_RPs,
          c("comp", "Description", "rank")]
    })) |> dplyr::mutate(structure = struct)
  })
)

if (nrow(rank_df) == 0) {
  message("No results available yet for rank heatmap.")
} else {

struct_order <- c("builtin_mm", pdbs)
rank_df$structure   <- factor(rank_df$structure,   levels = rev(struct_order))
rank_df$Description <- factor(rank_df$Description, levels = target_RPs)
rank_df$comp <- factor(rank_df$comp, levels = comp_labels,
                       labels = gsub("_", " ", comp_labels))

ggplot(rank_df, aes(x = Description, y = structure, fill = rank)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(!is.na(rank), as.character(rank), "")),
            size = 2.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ comp, nrow = 2) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "firebrick", high = "white",
                      na.value = "grey85", name = "Rank\n(1 = top)") +
  scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Rank of target RPs by ES2 (RPSEA.NES_randZ)",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.x    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
        axis.text.y    = element_text(size = 9),
        strip.text     = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
        panel.grid     = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "right")
}
```

## ES2 distribution across all structures

For each target RP, ES2 (RPSEA.NES\_randZ) is taken from its matched IP-vs-Total comparison
(`uL1_FLAG`, `eS25_FLAG`, `eL22_HA` vs their respective Total). "Others" shows the same
score for all remaining RPs in those three comparisons pooled. The dashed line marks ES2 = 1.

```{r es2-violin, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
matched_comps <- c(
  uL1  = "uL1_FLAG_vs_uL1_Total",
  eS25 = "eS25_FLAG_vs_eS25_Total",
  eL22 = "eL22_HA_vs_eL22_Total"
)

violin_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(results_list), function(struct) {
  res <- results_list[[struct]]
  if (is.null(res) || nrow(res) == 0) return(NULL)
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(matched_comps), function(rp) {
    sub <- dplyr::filter(res, comp == matched_comps[rp])
    if (nrow(sub) == 0) return(NULL)
    dplyr::transmute(sub,
      structure = struct,
      group = ifelse(Description == rp, rp, "Others"),
      ES2   = RPSEA.NES_randZ
    )
  }))
}))

violin_df$group <- factor(violin_df$group, levels = c("uL1", "eS25", "eL22", "Others"))

target_colors <- c(uL1 = "#d73027", eS25 = "#4575b4", eL22 = "#1a9850", Others = "grey70")

ggplot(violin_df, aes(x = group, y = ES2, fill = group)) +
  geom_violin(trim = TRUE, alpha = 0.6, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.12, size = 1.2, alpha = 0.5, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_hline(yintercept =  1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = target_colors, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "ES2 (RPSEA NES z-score)",
       title = "ES2 distribution across all structures",
       subtitle = "Matched IP-vs-Total comparisons; dashed lines at ES2 = ±1") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11))
```

# RP proximity set comparison

For structures where `gsea_sets_RP.rds` does not exist yet (older cached runs), the sets
are recomputed from the saved distance CSV. The built-in mouse sets come from
`ARF:::mouse_gsea_sets_RP`.

```{r rp-set-comparison, fig.width=12, fig.height=8, message=TRUE}
builtin_sets <- ARF:::mouse_gsea_sets_RP

# Collect sets: build from raw distance CSV + liftover if .rds is missing
all_sets <- list(builtin_mm = builtin_sets)
for (pdb in pdbs) {
  outdir_p  <- file.path(base_dir, pdb)
  sets_rds  <- file.path(outdir_p, "gsea_sets_RP.rds")
  dist_file <- file.path(outdir_p, paste0("Ribosome.3D.", pdb, ".ARF.minimum_distances.csv"))
  rrna_fasta <- file.path(outdir_p, paste0(pdb, ".rRNAs.fasta"))

  if (file.exists(sets_rds)) {
    all_sets[[pdb]] <- readRDS(sets_rds)
  } else if (file.exists(dist_file) && file.exists(rrna_fasta)) {
    tryCatch({
      LO_tmp <- .silent(ARF::ARF_convert_Ribo3D_pos(
        source_distance_file = dist_file,
        source_rRNAs_fasta   = rrna_fasta,
        target_species       = "mm",
        target_rRNAs_fasta   = mouse_rRNAs,
        type                 = "distances"
      ))
      s <- ARF::dripARF_get_RP_proximity_sets(
        RP_proximity_df   = LO_tmp,
        additional_RPcols = c(),
        rRNAs_fasta       = mouse_rRNAs
      )
      saveRDS(s, sets_rds)
      all_sets[[pdb]] <- s
      message(pdb, ": sets built and cached")
    }, error = function(e) message(pdb, ": set build failed — ", conditionMessage(e)))
  } else {
    message(pdb, ": no distance CSV available yet")
  }
}

# Compute set size and Jaccard overlap vs builtin_mm for each target RP
struct_order_sets <- c("builtin_mm", pdbs)
stats_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(all_sets), function(struct) {
  sets <- all_sets[[struct]]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(target_RPs, function(rp) {
    s       <- if (is.data.frame(sets))       sets$gene[sets$ont == rp]       else sets[[rp]]
    builtin <- if (is.data.frame(builtin_sets)) builtin_sets$gene[builtin_sets$ont == rp] else builtin_sets[[rp]]
    if (is.null(s) || length(s) == 0) return(NULL)
    n_s      <- length(s)
    n_b      <- length(builtin)
    n_int    <- if (length(builtin) > 0) length(intersect(s, builtin)) else NA_integer_
    n_uni    <- if (length(builtin) > 0) length(union(s, builtin))     else NA_integer_
    jaccard  <- if (!is.na(n_int) && n_uni > 0) n_int / n_uni       else NA_real_
    data.frame(structure = struct, RP = rp,
               set_size = n_s, overlap = n_int, jaccard = jaccard,
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
}))
if (!is.null(stats_df) && nrow(stats_df) > 0) {

stats_df$structure <- factor(stats_df$structure, levels = rev(struct_order_sets))
stats_df$RP        <- factor(stats_df$RP,        levels = target_RPs)

# Panel A: set sizes
p_size <- ggplot2::ggplot(stats_df, ggplot2::aes(x = RP, y = set_size, fill = structure)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(position = ggplot2::position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.7) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "RP proximity set size per structure",
                x = NULL, y = "Number of rRNA positions", fill = "Structure") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "right")

# Panel B: Jaccard similarity to builtin_mm
jaccard_df <- stats_df[stats_df$structure != "builtin_mm", ]
p_jaccard <- ggplot2::ggplot(jaccard_df,
                              ggplot2::aes(x = RP, y = structure, fill = jaccard)) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = ifelse(!is.na(jaccard),
                                                  sprintf("%.2f", jaccard), "")),
                     size = 2.8) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#2166ac",
                                limits = c(0, 1), na.value = "grey85",
                                name = "Jaccard\nvs builtin_mm") +
  ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Jaccard similarity of RP sets to builtin_mm",
                x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                 axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"))

gridExtra::grid.arrange(p_size, p_jaccard, ncol = 1, heights = c(1.2, 1))

} else {
  message("No set data available yet — re-knit after structures have been processed.")
}
```
